title: Instructor-designed AI improves learning in a randomized trial across 19 universities
abstract: arXiv:2611.19099v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Universities are alarmed by recent evidence that artificial intelligence (AI) can undermine learning, with students prescribed generic chatbots or centrally designed AI tools performing worse. In a pre-registered randomized controlled trial across 7,200 students at 19 universities over three semesters, we tested whether AI designed by frontline instructors can improve learning. We encouraged instructors to design AI solutions they believed would best help their students. Drawing on their unique knowledge of their classes and students, the instructors created a wide array of innovations. We show that these instructor-designed AI innovations improved student learning, measured by AI-proof assessments (proctored, in-person examinations). We found no change in student engagement, measured by course activity records, or satisfaction, measured by course evaluations. translated_title: 教师设计的AI在覆盖19所大学的随机对照试验中提升学习效果
translated_abstract: 大学界对近期关于人工智能（AI）可能损害学习的证据深感担忧，被分配使用通用聊天机器人或集中设计的AI工具的学生表现更差。在一项覆盖19所大学、7200名学生、历时三个学期的预注册随机对照试验中，我们测试了由一线教师设计的AI能否改善学习。我们鼓励教师设计他们认为最能帮助学生学习的AI方案。凭借对课堂和学生的独特了解，教师们创造出了丰富多样的创新方案。研究表明，这些教师设计的AI创新改善了学生的学习，学习效果通过防AI的评估方式（监考的线下考试）进行衡量。我们发现，学生的学习参与度（通过课程活动记录衡量）或满意度（通过课程评估衡量）没有发生变化。我们的研究结果表明，当AI的采用……
tldr: 该研究通过覆盖19所大学7200名学生的预注册随机对照试验证明，由一线教师根据自身课堂经验自主设计的AI工具能够切实提升学生学习效果，且提升效果经线下监考考试等防AI评估方式得到验证。
en_tdlr: A pre-registered randomized controlled trial across 7,200 students at 19 universities demonstrates that AI tools designed by frontline instructors improve student learning, as verified by AI-proof proctored in-person exams.
